clue.text: A call for help to install finest fibre insulation

indicators.note: the distress call is made to take in the other piece, so it sits around it

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
the finest is the best

explanation.surface: Someone in trouble calls for help to have the best insulation fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'install' suggests fitting insulation, but here the distress call simply holds the word for finest.
explanation.definitionFit: This mineral was once widely used as a fibrous heat-resistant lagging material.

clue.text: Part of Austria tends to be covered with ridges

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A region of Austria is described as tending to be mountainous and ridged.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb this means to mark with fine parallel grooves or stripes.

clue.text: One thus shows mushy demeanour?

indicators.note: mushy suggests something squashed to a pulp, so the letters of the following word are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A lovestruck person gives themselves away with a soppy, sentimental manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mushy' rearranges DEMEANOUR; the whole clue then describes someone smitten, who shows a mushy demeanour.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in love tends to behave in a soppy, sentimental way.

clue.text: Postgraduate has finally to put in this

definitions.text: Postgraduate has finally to put in this

indicators.note: the closing letters are placed into the middle of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A doctoral student is told what work must ultimately be submitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E and S, the last letters of 'Postgraduate' and 'has'; 'to put in' places them inside THIS. Read whole, the clue says what a postgraduate must submit.
explanation.definitionFit: A research student submits a long dissertation to gain a higher degree.

clue.text: Fading recollection of poor Tom Merry's mother

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters of the name and the word after it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Tom Merry's mother is suffering from a failing memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges all fifteen letters of TOM MERRYS MOTHER, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: The brief recall of recent facts is the kind that soon disappears.

clue.text: Key-cutting and copying done remotely

parts.note: F is a musical key
axing means cutting, as of jobs or costs

explanation.surface: A locksmith cuts keys and makes copies for customers who are not present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key-cutting' reads as a locksmith's trade, but splits into a key (F) and cutting.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending a facsimile transmits a copy of a document over a telephone line.

clue.text: Run around a little — it won't do much harm

indicators.note: the word for running is placed around the small amount

parts.note: to flee is to run away
a bit means a little

explanation.surface: A jogger is told a short run around will not be harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps FLEE round A BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's bite is a trivial injury, so the word also means a minor nuisance.

clue.text: Forceful in verbal inflection

parts.note: taken as written
tense is the inflection of a verb that marks time

explanation.surface: A speaker is described as forceful in the way their voice rises and falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbal inflection' sounds like tone of voice, but is grammar: the change in a verb's form showing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something strong, vehement and powerful in degree.

clue.text: Port wine to finish off

parts.note: Graves is a wine from the Bordeaux region of France
to end something is to finish it off

explanation.surface: A drinker reaches for the port with which to round off the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine; it is the definition, a town on the Thames estuary in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This Kent town on the Thames estuary is a harbour town, historically a shipping point.

clue.text: Sorting for quality — for instance, excellent — right to left

indicators.note: to left says the pieces are read leftwards, from the right, so the whole run goes backwards

parts.note: e.g. is short for exempli gratia, for instance
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as the letter I

explanation.surface: Goods are graded for quality, with the excellent ones moved from right to left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to left' turns EG + AI + RT, giving the answer read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The word now usually means prioritising patients, but originally meant grading produce by quality.

clue.text: To provide work for musicians, has to repeat broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of the phrase are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: To keep musicians employed, a show must be repeated on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges TOREPEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A light opera is a stage work performed by singers and an orchestra.

clue.text: Propeller of small boat that's on back in shed

indicators.note: the reversed pair is placed inside the word for shed

parts.note: to cast is to shed, as a snake casts its skin

indicators.note: back says the two words before it are read in reverse order

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone paddling a small boat has it upside down in a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text ended with a stray '18' that the printed page does not show; 'shed' is a verb, not an outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddler drives a light craft forward with a paddle.

clue.text: Black cat's lively manner

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the ounce is the snow leopard, a big cat; the 's is a link meaning has

explanation.surface: A black cat moves in a lively, sprightly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberance and energetic liveliness of character are this sense.

clue.text: Tantrum by Gunners that's lasted through half-time

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking or ill humour
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army

explanation.surface: A footballer sulks about the Gunners at the interval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunners' and 'half-time' suggest Arsenal football; the definition recalls the poem calling this Jordanian city 'rose-red' and 'half as old as time'.
explanation.definitionFit: John Burgon's poem calls the ancient Jordanian city 'a rose-red city half as old as time'.

clue.text: Teacher expected to come round eagerly after gym

indicators.note: after says the container follows the gym piece

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

indicators.note: the word for expected goes round the word for eager

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due
agog means eagerly expectant

explanation.surface: A teacher is due to arrive keenly after a gym session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gym' is school physical education, abbreviated as usual in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a slightly formal or pedantic term for a schoolmaster or instructor.

clue.text: I've many supporters giving money to try to stop losing millions

parts.note: a cent is a small coin, money

indicators.note: losing says the abbreviation is dropped from the word before

parts.note: to impede is to hinder, trying to stop
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Someone with many backers gives cash to prevent losing millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporters' are legs, which this creature has in great numbers; 'giving' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This arthropod has numerous legs, and the name means a hundred feet.

clue.text: Quiet conductor that produces grand sound

parts.note: piano is the musical direction for quiet
a wire conducts electricity

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken orchestral conductor creates a magnificent sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' suggests an orchestra leader, but is an electrical one; 'grand' is the grand piano.
explanation.definitionFit: The steel strings struck by hammers inside a grand make its tone.

clue.text: Painful condition caught during Asiatic trip

indicators.note: during says the abbreviation is placed within the rearranged letters
a trip is a stumble, so the letters of the word before are tripped into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A traveller develops a painful ailment while on a journey across Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges ASIATIC; 'during' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain along the sciatic nerve in the back and leg is this complaint.

clue.text: Book double act — one to appear in two months

parts.note: a duo is a pair of performers

indicators.note: the numeral is set inside the two month abbreviations

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
mo is short for month
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A comedy duo's book is due out within two months.
explanation.walkthrough: The book size is named for twelve, from the Latin for 'in twelfth'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a book size, made from sheets folded into twelve leaves.

clue.text: A folder is needed for this artistic work

definitions.text: A folder is needed for this artistic work

parts.words: A folder is needed for this artistic work
parts.note: a folder sounds like stationery, but here is a person creasing paper into shapes

explanation.surface: An art project calls for a document file.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese art makes figures by creasing a single sheet of paper.

clue.text: Father's bloody cut

parts.note: pa is father; the 's is a link meaning has
blood is red

explanation.surface: Father has a cut that bleeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Trimmed, as nails or vegetable skins are trimmed with a knife.

clue.text: Person of refined taste demanding pure ice in cocktail?

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of the phrase are mixed up

explanation.surface: A gourmet insists on pure ice in their drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in cocktail' rearranges PUREICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmet takes particular pleasure in fine food and wine.

clue.text: Last through is one encumbered by fat

indicators.note: the numeral is weighed down by, so held within, the word for fat

parts.note: stout means fat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone who is overweight is burdened when lasting the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'encumbered by' puts I inside STOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To endure until the end of something, or to stay seated rather than dance.

clue.text: Composer writing tie between adjacent notes

indicators.note: between places the word for tie between the two notes

parts.note: G and A are neighbouring notes of the scale
a link is a tie or connection

explanation.surface: A composer writes a tie, the curved mark joining two neighbouring notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' looks like the musical marking; it is LINK. 'between' sets it between G and A. Mikhail Glinka was a Russian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Glinka was a nineteenth-century Russian who wrote operas and orchestral music.

clue.text: Is party returning in Odyssey, for example, irregularly received?

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for a long heroic poem

parts.note: Homer's Odyssey is an epic poem
taken as written

indicators.note: returning says the word for party is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A guest returns to a party in Homer's tale and gets an irregular welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer's Odyssey stands for any long heroic poem, the category it belongs to.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sporadic arrives in separate instalments at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Flyers attack in turn — it's the writing on the wall

indicators.note: the pieces are placed inside the word for turn

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
the RAF is the Royal Air Force
a fit is an attack, as of coughing

explanation.surface: Airmen attack in turn, and the result is the writing on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flyers' are airmen collectively; the answer is the Italian singular of the familiar plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A single scribbled or painted inscription on a public wall is this, singular of a plural word.

clue.text: Repulsive swindle rejected financial undertakings

indicators.note: rejected says the word for swindle is turned back

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle them
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A nasty fraud has its promissory notes refused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DO into OD.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something hateful and disgusting.

clue.text: Scrambled German one could get right out of this machine

indicators.note: scrambled means jumbled, so the remaining letters are put into a new order
the abbreviation for right is taken out of the word for the nationality

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A coded German message could be decoded correctly using this device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes R from GERMAN, leaving GEMAN; add I and 'Scrambled' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The German cipher device used in the Second World War was famously cracked at Bletchley Park.

clue.text: Gossiped with newspaperman after treaty gets broken

indicators.note: after says the editor follows the rearranged letters
a broken treaty is shattered, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist gossiped once a peace accord was breached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newspaperman' is an editor, abbreviated in the crossword way.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter idly and at length is a synonym for chattering gossip.
